meta.name: vad-team-map20-v16
meta.description: VAD agent team v16 — settle the v167 CGR-M question with a CLEAN full-pipeline cgr-on vs cgr-off A/B, then promote or archive-close. Committed pipeline = v137 + BUE + CBT + CBT-recal (all default-ON, full-290 ~0.173); CGR-M (v167, --cgr_relocate) is code-present default-OFF. WHY THIS SESSION: v15 judged CGR with a paired field snapshotted PRE-BUE, so its +0.06105 "paired marginal" actually bundled BUE+CBT and was inflated. An offline reconstruction of the CGR-only step gave +0.01919 (P=0.886, CI90[-0.005,+0.051]) — promising but under the P>=0.90 bar, AND the offline method cannot see how BUE/CBT interact with a RELOCATED window (BUE grows from the new position; CBT clamps along a different curve region), which is exactly where CGR's real effect on FINAL mAP lives. v16 measures that interaction directly. KEY STRUCTURAL FACT (verified): CGR (pipeline.py ~L1790), CCR (~L1810), BUE (~L1818), CBT (~L1833) all run DOWNSTREAM of every VLM call, on cached motion-energy + CLIP curves — they are deterministic post-processing. So both A/B arms can be computed inside ONE eval run: arm-OFF = BUE+CBT applied to the pre-CGR detection snapshot; arm-ON = CGR then BUE+CBT. Same videos, same VLM outputs, same detection count -> an EXACT paired A/B with ZERO cross-run VLM noise, isolating CGR's true contribution to final mAP including the BUE/CBT interaction. The two arms differ by exactly one function call, so the comparison is sound by construction. CRITICAL IMPLEMENTATION HAZARD (verified): _cgr_motion_relocate / _bue_boundary_union_extension / _cbt_category_boundary_tighten all MUTATE a["t_start"]/a["t_end"] IN PLACE (pipeline.py L1298, L2174, L2378, L2532) — the dual-arm code MUST deep-copy the detection list before each arm or the arms corrupt each other. FALLBACK: if the dual-arm instrument fails its self-test, fall back to two REAL separate 88-video evals (cgr-on vs cgr-off) judged cross-run. Concurrency 2. All evals on the 88-video hard harness with --categories forced.
